static_proof.mutation_testing: Nine defect classes reintroduced one at a time. EIGHT are detected; M9 is NOT. Measured: reverting both captureOrReadTaskContract call sites in lane-start main() to a contract-less sync file leaves the four relevant suites at 115 tests, 115 pass, 0 fail. Nothing in this repository executes lane-start's main(); that was true before this lane and remains true. An earlier revision claimed 9 of 9 on the strength of a test that exercised the extracted helper rather than the wiring; that claim is withdrawn. Separately, the narrow compile smoke passed whenever tsc never ran; it is now hardened and verified by inversion.

premise_verification.claim: The replaced codex dry-run test could not observe the packet layer.
premise_verification.method: Restored the replaced test verbatim from 581af41bf145f17dea8cfae4966c799f58077748, applied the M1 defect (dry run takes the capturing path), ran the suite.
premise_verification.result: The replaced test PASSED with the defect present, while both new mutation-sensitive tests FAILED.
premise_verification.why: It named an issue with no manifest on disk, so main() exited at the manifestExists guard; a 'no manifest found' refusal satisfies every one of its assertions.

isolation.mechanism: getRepoRoot() (scripts/ops/shared.ts:463) runs `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` with no cwd option, inheriting process.cwd(). Executing an entrypoint as a child process with cwd inside a git-initialised fixture directory rebinds ROOT to it for the whole run.
isolation.offline_mechanism: Stub codex/claude CLIs on PATH satisfy the health checks; the stub bin directory is kept outside the fixture git repository so it is not untracked content.
isolation.verified: docs/06_status/lanes and .ops/sync in the live checkout contain no UTV2-9999xx fixture after the full suite runs.

defect.root_cause: execution-packet.ts is reached only through two entrypoints whose main() functions were effectively untested. codex-exec.ts calls process.exit() at 19 sites and shells out to the real codex CLI for its health check, so an in-process test could neither survive it nor run it offline; the existing test avoided both by never getting far enough to matter.
defect.second_defect: The two claude dry-run tests did reach packet generation, but wrote their lane manifest and sync record into the live checkout at ROOT. An interrupted run leaves those behind, and the concurrency governor reads a stray manifest in docs/06_status/lanes as a real active lane.
defect.third_defect: The inherited control-character test asserted a property that held trivially for its own fixture.

safety_posture.behavioural_change_1: lane-start now requires a reachable Linear and a valid token on every lane start and resume. Fails closed (structured lane_start_failed, exit 1) before lease reservation or worktree creation, so it cannot orphan state, but it is a new failure mode under containment and in CI.
safety_posture.behavioural_change_2: Asymmetric root on resume: syncContentWithTaskContract merges against ROOT/.ops/sync/<id>.yml but the resume path writes into the lane worktree. Measured: 481 of 481 sync records in the root checkout carry no task_contract, so every resume merge base is legacy - branch-accumulated entities are overwritten and the contract can be re-fetched and swapped mid-flight. Inherited from 581af41b; disclosed, not fixed.
safety_posture.correction: An earlier revision of this bundle asserted production_behaviour_changed: false. That was wrong relative to main and is withdrawn.

pending: M9 (lane-start main() capture wiring) has no executing coverage - disclosed, not closed.
Two Tier C behavioural changes inherited from the port require a PM decision: the new hard Linear dependency on every lane start/resume, and the asymmetric-root overwrite on resume.

known_limitations: The fixture helpers are duplicated across claude-exec.test.ts and codex-exec.test.ts rather than shared. This lane may not add a file, and importing a helper from another test module would re-register that module's tests in both runs. Recorded as a visible decision, not an oversight.

The codex dry-run prompt preview is truncated before the objective renders, so the codex test ties the prompt to the on-disk contract by integrity hash instead of matching the objective text directly. The claude preview does include the objective and is asserted directly.
Each executing test spawns a tsx child process and costs roughly 0.8s; the three executor suites run in about 6s total.

The packet parser's heading whitelist does not cover '## Deliverables' or '## Hard constraints', which UTV2-1736 uses. Content is preserved verbatim via unmapped_sections and no field falsely claims 'none declared', so this is a extraction-quality follow-up, not a correctness defect.

Nothing in the repository executes lane-start's main(). Closing M9 honestly needs a child-process test against a fixture root requiring a preflight token, a git repository, worktree creation and pnpm install - better as its own increment.

carry_forward_audit.scope: All eight script files from rejected PR #1445, compared by SHA-256 against current main, preserved head 581af41b, and this worktree.
carry_forward_audit.finding: lane-start.ts and lane-start.test.ts were accidentally omitted. They are the capture step: on main, lane-start writes a sync record with no task_contract, and readTaskContract throws 'task contract is absent' for every real lane.
carry_forward_audit.precision_correction: Capture is NOT absent altogether. The exec-time path (generateDispatchExecutionPacketResult) still captures and persists at dispatch. The omission specifically breaks the DRY-RUN path, which deliberately never captures - so without lane-start-time capture, every --dry-run on a real lane refuses. That is the exact path this lane's new tests exercise.
